lines.text: She does not turn around.
She hears the door close and the footsteps draw nearer.
Dorothy lowers her head and closes her eyes. A silent signal that she doesn't want to be spoken to.
Then, a familiar scent reaches her.
The scent of marigold.
*Click*
She hears a teacup being placed in front of her,
and the sound of the chair across from her being pulled out and someone sitting in it.
A brief silence ensues.
Then the sound of tea being sipped from across the table is heard.
Dorothy opens her eyes.
She looks at the golden liquid swirling in the teacup.
After letting out a short sigh, Dorothy reaches for the cup.
Just as she is about to grasp the handle, a voice speaks from across the table.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Hmm. Nothing beats a good cup of tea.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I see you're still as picky as ever.
Dorothy freezes and her pupils widen.
She barely manages to lift her trembling head to look forward.
Andersen looks at Dorothy with a gentle smile.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Miss Dorothy.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Com...mander...

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Thank goodness. I was worried you might not recognize me now that I'm older.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: How...
Dorothy's thoughts come to a halt.
How many times in the past has she been manipulated by ghosts from her past.
First Liliweiss, then Pinne.
Wariness fills Dorothy's eyes.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: ... Who are you?
Andersen silently looks at Dorothy.
Dorothy silently looks back at Andersen.
After staring at one another for a long time, Dorothy becomes certain.
He is not an illusion, nor a monster wearing another's skin.
He's the same person she once knew, bearing the marks of time on his face.
The same person who shared her most radiant days.
Tears fall from Dorothy's eyes.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: You're... alive...

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Ta-da. I'm still alive and kicking.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: *Sob*

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I'm sorry I couldn't come see you sooner.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: But you've gotta admit, reuniting in a prison visitation room is quite dramatic.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: *Sob*

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: The things you get to see when you live long enough.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: To think that such a noble lady would end up in a cell.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: The others would get a real kick out of this.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: *Sob*

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: You haven't changed at all. There's a bit more intensity in your eyes, but you're exactly the same.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Maybe I should have become a Nikke too. I'm the only one aging here, it's ridiculous.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Do you have some kind of skincare routine? Care to share it with me?

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Please...! Be quiet!

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Can't you see... I'm crying right now...!

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Stop crying, or you'll get me started too.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: The older I get, the easier the tears come. It's becoming quite the problem.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I've been taking all sorts of things for my health, but nothing's quite what it used to be.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Please...! Just...! Keep it down...!

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: *Sigh* Honestly.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I told you not to cry.
Only the sound of Dorothy's sobs echoes through the visitation room.
Dorothy brings the tea to her lips.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Not bad at all. The leaves are good, and it's well-brewed.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Look at you, pretending to be elegant when you were just bawling your eyes out two seconds ago.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: ... How long are you going to keep bringing that up?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Let me see. Until I get to tell Lilith?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I already know.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: That damned Queen stole Lilith's body.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: That thing needs to die. Without a doubt.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: But what are you doing here right now?

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: ... You must have already heard everything.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Yes. That's why I'm asking.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: You could be out there right now trying to tear the Queen's head off. So what are you doing sitting here?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: On a journey of self-discovery, are you?

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: I could say the same thing about you, Commander!

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: You were alive this whole time! What were you doing?!

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: And despite me already being in the Ark, why did you wait until now to...!

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Calm down. I'll explain everything.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Hmm... It's been a while since I talked about the old days. My heart's racing.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Quit kidding around!

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: First of all...

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: During Operation Ark Guardian, I was on the brink of death, when Lilith forcibly sent me into the Ark.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I've always felt terrible about leaving without saying goodbye. I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I arrived at the Ark and I received treatment, somehow managing to cling on to life.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: By the time I woke up, decades had passed.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Those V.T.C. bastards had forcibly induced me into a coma for all those years.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Good grief. I'm sure that technology was never designed to be used as such.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: So... V.T.C. did that... to keep you in check.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Yes. You heard that from Burningum?

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: No. I read it in the book.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Ah, that book. It's quite well written. Though it skims through my exploits a bit too much for my liking. But it was a fine book.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Anyway, after sleeping like the dead for all those years, it was thanks to a man named Arthur that I finally woke up.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: When I came to, my body was a wreck, and you were all, bizarrely, being called Pilgrims.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I did some digging and used every connection I had to investigate why things ended up like this.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I eventually found the culprit. It was V.T.C., a painfully obvious conclusion.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: After getting myself back in shape, I heard there was an event where key figures would gather.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: So I went and paid them a little visit.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: You killed them all.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Yes, I did. I let the leader escape though.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: My achievement was recognized... Hah. Even though it's an achievement for eliminating political enemies.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I even rose to the position of Deputy Chief.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: After that, I tried tirelessly to find all of you.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: But you were just too good at running away, there was no way to catch any of you.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: And though your personalities had changed somewhat...

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: You were still out there, fighting for humanity.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I desperately wanted to go up there myself, but my body couldn't last a day without specialized treatment.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: And considering the mortality rates up on the surface, sending someone else up was too risky a proposition.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: So I left things as they were.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I simply issued a directive not to attack any Pilgrim since they are friendly to humanity, and to request their help instead.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Still, you could have tried at least once.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: How could I possibly face any of you.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I fled to the Ark at the end of Operation Ark Guardian,

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: and left you stranded for decades.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: The fact that I was sent here against my will doesn't change that fact.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: So I decided to simply watch over you and help from a distance.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Because the me that I am now is someone with authority without the ability to act.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Even so...!

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I wanted to see you.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: But... well... I couldn't.
Andersen lightly taps his side with his fist.
A metallic thud echoes.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I can no longer be the commander who charges into battle alongside you.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: It's embarrassing.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: So after stepping back from the front lines, I did what I could to help with surface reclamation efforts.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I cleaned up the mess we had for a military, rewrote our combat manuals... I worked quite hard, in whatever way I could.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: But things were a disaster. After two failed surface reclamation wars, the Ark was in shambles.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: So I've been managing the fallout ever since, right up to now.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Well then. I suppose that covers my sob story.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: You're wondering why I never came to see you after you got to the Ark, aren't you?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: After all, you made such a flashy entrance, appearing like an angel from above. There's no way I wouldn't have known.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Yes. Let's hear it.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I knew everything about your situation.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I knew better than anyone why you'd come to the Ark.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: That's why I stayed away.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: What on earth are you saying?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Because if you had asked me to destroy the Ark together, I would have agreed.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I would have smashed the Ark with you and cheered for Eden.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: The Ark matters. Like it or not, it is humanity's last refuge.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: It must be protected at all costs.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: That is why I went to Burningum.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: He has a sharp eye for people, and good instincts. He's a talented man with no flaws, aside from his weight.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I asked him to determine your true intentions.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: If you were still the same as before, the Ark would help you.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: But if you were truly intent on destroying the Ark...

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: You told him to kill me?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: You would do that to me?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: The hero who is forced to cut down a fallen comrade. Talk about a cliché.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: On the other hand.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: The hero who sides with his fallen comrade and joins the Demon King's army.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: That's also not terribly original.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I'm glad you haven't changed.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Commander.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: I've changed a lot.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: You're the same.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I'm convinced of that.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: You put on that tough act all by yourself,

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: but in the end, you're guided by your heart and you sacrifice yourself for the greater good.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Stand with the Ark, Dorothy.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Let's go kill that Queen. Just thinking about that bitch keeps me awake at night.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Yes. After sharpening your teeth on revenge for so long, it won't be easy.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: But Dorothy.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: The reason you never put your plans into action,

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: means you never truly intended to see them through.
*Vrrr*

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Hmm. Excuse me for a moment.
Andersen takes out his phone.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Yes, it's me.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Mmm, yes. I'll return shortly. I'm meeting an old acquaintance.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: My condition has been stable, so I don't see why I need such frequent checkups.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Understood. I'll be there soon.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Yes. See you later.
*Beep*

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: ... Your way of speaking has changed a lot.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I'm a Deputy Chief, after all. I have to act a little dignified.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: But I'm the same man I was before.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: My body may be broken down and aging, but my heart is unchanged.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: What about you?

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: I have to go, but I'll be back.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: Listen to the guard and don't try to escape.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: ... Commander.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Despite all that's happened,

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: I'm glad I could see you again.

lines.speaker: andersen
lines.text: See? I told you I tear up easily now that I'm getting older.

lines.speaker: anis_i_w
lines.text: Oh, try these. They're apparently mint chocolate seafood chips.

lines.speaker: neon_v_w
lines.text: Yuck. What unholy abomination is that?

lines.speaker: rapi_red
lines.text: Sounds like a gourmet, haute cuisine snack.

lines.speaker: rapi_red
lines.text: Let Dorothy be the judge. She has discerning taste.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: I'm not eating that.
Wow, this fried ramen is really good. It's salty, spicy, and just hits the spot.

lines.speaker: anis_i_w
lines.text: It's good. I think it tanked because of its name. Change that and it would be a hit.

lines.speaker: rapi_red
lines.text: Why did you buy so many dumplings?

lines.speaker: neon_v_w
lines.text: The shop's grill was fired up to the max. With firepower like that, it can't taste all that bad.

lines.speaker: neon_v_w
lines.text: Dorothy, want to give it a sniff? It's got this great smokiness.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: No, thank you.

lines.speaker: rapi_red
lines.text: Then what about this? It's called flower bread. There's red bean paste inside.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Why would a flower bread have red bean paste in it?

lines.speaker: rapi_red
lines.text: Beats me. Maybe because it's shaped like a flower?
Now that you mention it, there are a lot of different breads like that. Fish-shaped bread, for example.

lines.speaker: neon_v_w
lines.text: Oh! I read in a book that they used to put real fish in fish bread.

lines.speaker: anis_i_w
lines.text: What kind of weird books are you even reading?

lines.speaker: anis_i_w
lines.text: By the way, Dorothy, why aren't you eating? We bought all this for you.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: You say that, but all of you seem to be doing the eating.

lines.speaker: anis_i_w
lines.text: Because you're refusing everything even if we spoon-feed you!

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: You haven't spoon-fed me anything yet.

lines.speaker: anis_i_w
lines.text: Fine, then open wide and say aaahhh!

lines.speaker: anis_i_w
lines.text: See? Even if we spoon-feed you, you won't eat.

lines.speaker: neon_v_w
lines.text: Then feed me instead! Aaaaah!

lines.speaker: anis_i_w
lines.text: There.

lines.speaker: neon_v_w
lines.text: Blech! Why did you stick your fingers in?!

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: ... Since you are done eating, could you leave now?
We haven't even started.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: *Sigh*
30 minutes later...

lines.speaker: anis_i_w
lines.text: Ah, that was delicious.

lines.speaker: rapi_red
lines.text: Shall we get going then?

lines.speaker: neon_v_w
lines.text: Yeah, let's grab some coffee on the way. I feel like I'm gonna burst.
Oh, Dorothy, be sure to eat the crème brûlée today. Otherwise, it'll spoil.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: ... Are you really leaving?
Hmm? Yeah, we finished eating, after all.

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: Did you not come because you had something to say?

lines.speaker: rapi_red
lines.text: The truth is, we're here because Anis wanted to see you in a prison uniform.

lines.speaker: anis_i_w
lines.text: Hey! You said you wanted to see it too!

lines.speaker: neon_v_w
lines.text: But how are your clothes so clean after all this time in here? Do you sleep standing up?

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: *Sigh* All right. Please leave.

lines.speaker: rapi_red
lines.text: Do you have any letters you want delivered? People in prison tend to write a lot of letters to the outside.

lines.speaker: anis_i_w
lines.text: Oh, right. Rapi is an ex-convict, so she knows all about this stuff. If there's anything you don't know, ask her.

lines.speaker: rapi_red
lines.text: I made a brief mistake... during my turbulent youth...

lines.speaker: neon_v_w
lines.text: Then if you and Dorothy ended up in the same squad, does that make it a criminal squad?

lines.speaker: anis_i_w
lines.text: Isn't that the story with everyone in Real Kindness?

lines.speaker: dorothy
lines.text: ... Please get out.
